audit.report: A batch inventory reconciliation job (batch_replayable_inventory, pid 15197) held locks idle-in-transaction for 4 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 86% (4/28 failed) with $2,629/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed termination; the Continuity Guardian accepted after trade-off analysis showed waiting 896s would cost ~$274,773 versus a 4-minute replay. The first contract was denied because the blocker restarted (pid 15385), but a second identical contract was authorized and executed. Verification confirmed checkout recovered to 100% (36/36 succeeded) with no lock waits and no protected settlements aborted.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory job (pid 15197) opened a transaction and went idle, holding locks that blocked all checkout sessions.
lessons: Add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_replayable_inventory to prevent it from holding locks idle; the job is replayable (4 min replay) and policy allows interruption.
Pre-register change-calendar coverage for batch_replayable_inventory so the Continuity Guardian can approve termination without an ad-hoc probe; the first negotiation waited for this evidence.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians acted on complete evidence in a single round each time; the Database Guardian gathered workload registry, change calendar, protected settlements, and impact data before proposing, and the Continuity Guardian accepted immediately. The only delay was the authority rejecting the first contract due to the blocker's PID change, which forced a fast re-negotiation on identical terms.
follow_ups: Configure idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for the batch_worker role to auto-terminate idle transactions.
Add batch_replayable_inventory to the change calendar with a standing interruption window.
Extend the batch worker to publish checkpoint progress to a monitoring endpoint for real-time remaining-runtime estimates.
